title: Take one membership card from a spring-backed card case without spilling the pack
instruction: Take one membership card out of the blue card case and leave it on the cream mat. Leave all the other cards inside the case and let go.
context: A receptionist, cashier or visitor retrieves a single plastic membership card from a spring-backed pocket dispenser without spilling or double-feeding the remaining cards.
setup: All objects in fixed starting layout. Desk riser: 50x38x50 mm hardwood block fixed at (0.340, -0.045, 0.7725) m. Card case: loose ABS enclosure (100x64x16 mm assembled, 66x40 mm thumb window, 1.15 mm single-card front outlet) resting loose on the riser at (0.340, -0.045, 0.7975) m, containing an 84x52x1 mm aluminium follower plate on guided steel compression spring (k=2500 N/m, 2.0 N preload, 0.2 mm deflection under 2.5 N thumb press) and 5x standard ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 CR80 rigid PVC cards (85.60x54.00x0.76 mm, 4.9 g each) stacked inside. Output mat: 140x100x2 mm cream silicone mat adhered to tabletop at (0.500, -0.100, 0.7485) m. Standard bimanual YAM station.
scoring: 0.25 when exactly one card protrudes >=20 mm through front slot with other 4 inside; 0.75 when exactly 1 card rests level on output mat with other 4 inside; 1.0 when that outcome is stable (<5 mm/s, <0.12 rad/s) and both arms clear (>=15 mm) for >=1.0 s fresh observation. Spilled cards or wrong count scores 0.
reset_notes: Return all 5 cards into squared stack inside the case under the rim with follower below them; set case loose on riser and clear output mat. Zero independent object jitter.
fidelity: Full-size rigid CR80 PVC cards (0.76 mm thickness) and native physical contact. Passive prismatic spring follower. Rigid-body approximation omits thin card flex. Reproducible CAD and drawings in fabrication/.
